title: Latria and dulia, with hyperdulia for Mary, though Scripture does not keep the distinction exactly
source_text: III. Ut vero cultus ille facilius posset a divino distingui, Scholas utrumque cultum proprio quodam nomine signavisse: & divino cultui quidem Latriae vocem, illi vero qui Sanctis Angelis & hominibus debetur, Dulia nomen appropriavisse. Quae Dulia rursus distinguitur in Hyperduliam, quae Beatae Virgini, & Duliam proprie sic dictam, quae Sanctis reliquis competit: quamvis agnoscant in Scripturae usu discrimen istud inter Latriam & Duliam exacte non servari.
pass_a_gloss: So that that cult might more easily be distinguished from the divine cult, the Schools marked each cult with a certain proper name: the word Latria for the divine cult, and the name Dulia for the cult owed to holy angels and men. Dulia is again divided into Hyperdulia, which belongs to the Blessed Virgin, and Dulia properly so called, which belongs to the remaining Saints: although they acknowledge that in the use of Scripture that difference between Latria and Dulia is not exactly kept.
pass_b_english: The Schools coined Latria for worship of God and Dulia for honor of holy angels and people.
Dulia is then split: Hyperdulia for the Blessed Virgin, and Dulia in the strict sense for the other Saints.
They admit Scripture itself does not keep that Latria–Dulia split with exactness.

choices.why: Names the higher dulia Rome assigns to Mary, not a third divine cult.
